content.title: About
content.content: Cauliflower is a cruciferous vegetable that, after harvesting, is blanched, flash‑frozen and enriched with added fat to improve flavor and texture. The product is ready to eat after heating and retains most of the nutrients found in fresh cauliflower.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cauliflower is rich in B‑vitamins, vitamin C and dietary fiber.
Freezing preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C, which is lost during prolonged storage of fresh heads.
Added fat enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
It is a staple in low‑calorie diets because of its low energy density and high fiber content.
In some regions cauliflower is colloquially called “white cabbage.”

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress and strengthening the immune system.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Cholesterol reduction
items.content: Phytochemicals in cauliflower help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Weight management
items.content: Low calorie content and high satiety make it suitable for weight‑control diets.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to cauliflower.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: The added fat should be considered by those monitoring their fat intake.

items.title: Moisture formation
items.content: Improper storage can lead to ice crystal formation, affecting texture after reheating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the product by steaming, microwaving, or boiling for 5–7 minutes. Serve as a side dish, add to soups, stews, casseroles, or blend into a puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw and refreeze.
